snippet.title: Allen Stanford's $7 Billion Ponzi Scheme: The Rise and Fall of a Caribbean Empire
snippet.description:
Allen Stanford wasn't just a banker; he was a knight, a billionaire, and the owner of a private island. He was also running the second-largest Ponzi scheme in history, right behind Bernie Madoff. For two decades, he sold certificates of deposit with "guaranteed" returns that didn't exist, using the money to fund a lifestyle of jets, cricket tournaments, and mansions.

Discover how he bribed auditors, fooled the SEC for years, and how a few brave whistleblowers finally brought him down. This is the story of how easy it is to buy credibility if you have enough stolen cash.

This story of fake profits is strikingly similar to the Luckin Coffee scandal. Watch how they faked $300 million in sales here: https://youtu.be/BL1kNPVxwjw

Paradise is easy to sell when you're paying for it with other people's money.

snippet.title: The European Kings Club: The Ponzi Scheme That Fooled Switzerland & Germany
snippet.description:

snippet.title: Investigating Bukele and Trump’s Controversial CECOT Deal | FRONTLINE (PBS) + @elfaro
snippet.description:
Three months after President Donald Trump returned to office in 2025 and began his major immigration crackdown, he held a White House sit-down with a popular Latin American leader who had once called himself the world’s coolest dictator. Watch the opening scene of “The Deal: Trump, Bukele & the Gangs of El Salvador,” a new documentary from FRONTLINE and El Faro. 

This journalism is made possible by viewers like you. Donate to FRONTLINE now: https://bit.ly/47DFzCb

And support your local PBS station here: https://www.pbs.org/donate

As the documentary explores, Bukele opened the doors of the notorious Salvadoran prison known as CECOT to planeloads of mostly Venezuelan U.S. deportees that the Trump administration had swept up and accused of being gang members. Later reporting would reveal that most of the men had no criminal convictions in the U.S. or proven gang affiliations.

“It was pretty obvious what Trump was getting out of this deal,” T. Christian Miller of ProPublica says in the opening scene. “It was much less obvious what Bukele was doing.”

That lack of transparency was familiar to Carlos Martínez and Óscar Martínez, reporters at the El Salvador investigative news outlet El Faro who have covered Bukele and his administration for years.

“The nature of Bukele’s government is to keep things secret,” Carlos says in the opening scene. 

FRONTLINE and El Faro’s documentary, releasing April 7, pierces that veil to investigate what underpinned Bukele’s controversial CECOT deal with the Trump administration. The film chronicles how the brothers and their colleagues discovered evidence that ran counter to Bukele’s tough-on-gangs image: Bukele’s government had previously negotiated with MS-13 and other violent gangs it publicly claimed to be cracking down on, El Faro found. Those negotiations, documents showed, involved offering privileges to gang leaders in prison, in exchange for a reduction in homicides and voter support in territories the gangs controlled.

Following the revelations, Bukele, who had vowed to end government corruption and crush gangs, claimed “El Faro lied” and said the documents showing his administration’s dealings with gang leaders were “fake.” The Martínez brothers now live — and report — in exile.

Through the brothers’ story, as well as the perspectives of other reporters, former U.S. officials and insiders, “The Deal” shines new light on Bukele’s tangled history with the gangs the U.S. is fighting. The documentary examines why Bukele offered to imprison U.S. deportees in CECOT — and why, in exchange, he asked for a number of gang leaders in U.S. custody to be returned to El Salvador, in what one reporter in the documentary calls “a deal within a deal.”

Bukele has said the Trump administration's return of MS-13 members will help El Salvador "finalize intelligence gathering and go after the last remnants" of the gang. But some observers suspect he had another motive: preventing gang leaders in U.S. custody from exposing the details of their past dealings with Bukele’s administration. 

For the full story, watch “The Deal: Trump, Bukele & the Gangs of El Salvador.”

******
Tyler1 is known today as a popular streamer on the Twitch platform, and a player of the popular online video game League of Legends (created by the company Riot Games). 

Others may know him from the various "rage compilation" and "meme compilation" videos of him spread out across YouTube and other platforms that have garnered millions of views. 

But before Tyler1's brand became as established as it is today, and before Tyler1 was known for his entertainment, he was initially classed as "the most toxic League of Legends player in North America". People only recognised Tyler for his toxic behaviour in the League of Legends community.

Tyler1's story was something quite surreal to have witnessed, especially for those who had first seen his rise to fame initially through Disco Heat's video on Tyler1.

Disco Heat's video had propelled Tyler1's audience into the thousands. It also highlighted his toxic behaviour in the game, and spawned copycats that would mimic Tyler1's attitude and behaviour whilst playing League of Legends.  

What ensued afterwards was a rare "indefinite ban" punishment by Riot Games, and a battle between Tyler1 as a brand and Riot Games as a company. 

This brought Tyler1's brand to a standstill and an all important realisation: that if Tyler1 was to maintain his audience and streaming career, he would have to be known for something other than his toxic behaviour. He would have to create a "redemption arc" for his brand, and eclipse the negative associations of his current brand. 

What followed was a series of entertaining and special events throughout Tyler1's streaming career that allowed him to craft memorable moments that would define his brand amongst the streaming community of Twitch. 

Tyler1’s story and journey as a brand displayed how a personal brand is built on a persons’ experience of you. Change their experience and you change the brand. It isn’t about the followers, nor is it about exposure. Your brand is built from the moment you interact with someone else.

In this documentary, we explore the complete story of Gary McKinnon, the Pentagon hack, his claims about secret UFO files, the evidence he says he discovered, and the legal fight that nearly resulted in his extradition to the United States.

Was he a dangerous cybercriminal who compromised national security?

Or an obsessive truth-seeker who exposed serious weaknesses in government computer systems?

Watch and decide for yourself.

Last week, the White House decided to pivot from "America First" to "America Everywhere." It began on Saturday morning with a 150-aircraft military strike to serve what Secretary of State Marco Rubio described as a "routine law enforcement warrant"—proving once and for all that if you have a large enough aircraft carrier, every parking ticket is technically a tactical operation.

In this video, we look at the internal contradictions of the new "Donroe Doctrine," a policy that treats international borders as suggested boundaries and sovereign nations as distressed assets. We explore why the plan to "take the oil" faces a minor mathematical hurdle: according to Rystad Energy, 60% of Venezuela's production projects require an oil price of $80 per barrel just to break even. This makes the administration's plan to lower gas prices by flooding the market with oil a bit like trying to save money on your commute by buying a fleet of private jets.

We also look at the high-profile residents currently moving into the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn, why the "ultimate sin" in modern diplomacy is keeping your own Nobel Peace Prize, and why the Danish government is currently checking its lease agreement on Greenland after being told the U.S. is interested in a "hard way" to close the deal.

snippet.title: Trump’s Inner Circle & Use of Military Power | The War Cabinet (full documentary) | FRONTLINE (PBS)
snippet.description:
A 90-minute documentary examining the key players behind President Trump’s expansive use of the U.S. military during his second term. 

This journalism is made possible by viewers like you. Donate to FRONTLINE now: https://bit.ly/47DFzCb

And support your local PBS station here: https://www.pbs.org/donate

When Donald Trump campaigned for his second term, he made a repeated promise: no new wars.

Drawing on in-depth interviews with President Trump’s allies and associates, officials from his first administration, and his critics, as well as former diplomats, military experts and journalists, “The War Cabinet” traces how, after vowing to end wars, not start them, Trump assembled a team of loyalists, and together they pursued a much different course. 

That team includes Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, longtime aide Stephen Miller, Chief of Staff Susie Wiles, Vice President JD Vance and outgoing Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard. The documentary tells the story of how the cabinet, a group whose members had diverse life stories and worldviews, came together to support the president in his quest to demonstrate the United States’ military might on the international stage.

The film traces how Trump has increasingly sought to cement his legacy and achieve U.S. policy objectives through military strength; how the administration has engaged militarily everywhere from Yemen, to the waters off Venezuela, to Iran; and the roles of key players in Trump’s second-term military decisions. With the Iran conflict now in its third month and threatening to define Trump’s second term, “The War Cabinet” is a must-watch documentary on how the president who promised peace has become a wartime president — and the ongoing ramifications.

snippet.title: They Hacked Roulette With the World's First Wearable Computer
snippet.description:
In 1978, a 26-year-old physics PhD student and a group of friends attempted something that sounded impossible: they built the world's first wearable computer, hid it inside a shoe, and used it to predict roulette spins in Las Vegas casinos.

Long before smartphones, smartwatches, or modern wearable tech existed, these young scientists were secretly carrying a custom-built computer powerful enough to calculate the physics of a spinning roulette wheel in real time. Their goal wasn't luck—it was science.

This is the incredible true story of J. Doyne Farmer and the Eudaemons, a group of physicists who challenged the idea that roulette was purely random. Armed with mathematics, electronics, and a revolutionary invention hidden inside a shoe, they set out to beat one of the most iconic casino games in the world.

From years of experimentation and engineering challenges to secret casino operations and the birth of wearable computing, this story sits at the fascinating intersection of science, technology, gambling, and human ingenuity.

snippet.title: The Scam That Fooled Every Casino in Vegas- Richard Marcus and the Savannah Scam
snippet.description:
How did one man fool casinos around the world using nothing more than a casino chip?

Richard Marcus wasn't a hacker, a card counter, or a mathematical genius. He was a former casino dealer who discovered a weakness hidden in plain sight: human psychology. Using a technique known as the Savannah Scam, Marcus and his team reportedly won millions from casinos by exploiting dealer assumptions, distractions, and split-second moments of confusion.

In this documentary, we uncover the incredible true story of Richard Marcus, the infamous casino cheat who pulled off one of the most brilliant gambling scams in history. From his early days inside the casino industry to the development of the legendary Savannah Scam, this is the story of how a simple chip-handling trick challenged some of the most secure gambling establishments in the world.

Discover:
 How the Savannah Scam worked
 The casino chip trick that generated massive payouts
 Why casinos struggled to detect the scam
 The psychology behind deception and misdirection
 How casino security eventually adapted
 What happened to Richard Marcus after his cheating career

This story isn't just about gambling—it's about perception, confidence, and one of the most fascinating cons ever documented.

In January 2014, a major poker tournament at Borgata Casino in Atlantic City descended into chaos when officials discovered something almost impossible to believe: millions of dollars worth of counterfeit poker chips had been secretly introduced into the event.

At the center of the scandal was Christian Lusardi, a relatively unknown poker player who allegedly used fake chips to gain an advantage in the Borgata Winter Poker Open. What began as a suspicious chip count soon turned into one of the most bizarre investigations in gambling history—one that ultimately led authorities to a clogged toilet filled with counterfeit poker chips.

This documentary explores the complete story behind Christian Lusardi's infamous $2.7 million counterfeit chip scheme, the investigation that exposed it, the impact on the tournament's remaining players, and how one of poker's biggest scandals unraveled in spectacular fashion.

snippet.title: He Stole the Soviet Union's Most Secret Jet and Escaped
snippet.description:
In 1953, a young North Korean fighter pilot made a decision that stunned the world.

No Kum-sok climbed into a Soviet-built MiG-15—one of the most secret and feared fighter jets of the Cold War—and flew it straight into South Korea. In just 17 minutes, he delivered America's most wanted aircraft, embarrassed North Korea and the Soviet Union, and changed military aviation history forever.

But this wasn't a mission ordered by intelligence agencies. It was a daring escape by a man willing to risk everything for freedom.

This documentary tells the incredible true story of the Korean War pilot who defected with a top-secret MiG-15, the CIA's desperate efforts to obtain one, Operation Moolah, and how a single flight gave the United States access to one of the Soviet bloc's greatest military secrets.

From Cold War espionage and aerial combat to political intrigue and personal courage, this is one of the most remarkable defections in aviation history.
